A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Intrinsic Image Fusion, with readable main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. The earlier supplementary Figures 9–13 can be matched to Figures 12–16 in v2, supporting reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and the appendix report original synthetic and real-scene reconstructions, quantitative baseline comparisons in Table 1, and ablation results in Tables 2–3.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds temperature-sensitivity and geometry-comparison results in supplementary Figures 9–10.

M1.justification: The affine material parameterization, Laplacian distribution matching and inverse-path-tracing fitting procedure are unchanged. The temperature ablation examines the existing procedure; the selected annealing factor of 0.85 was already specified in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions cover synthetic indoor scenes, ScanNet++ and FIPT real scenes, already including laser-scanned and photometrically reconstructed geometry. V2 adds another ScanNet++ scene and a controlled comparison of those existing geometry types within the retained task and domain.

E2.justification: NeILF++, FIPT and IRIS remain the reconstruction baselines, and the RGBX, per-object and per-texel aggregation comparisons are retained. IRIS is cited as a geometry source in the new geometry ablation, rather than introduced as a new reconstruction comparator.

E3.justification: New experiments compare annealing factors 0.75, 0.85 and 0.95 using assignment-entropy trajectories, and compare laser versus photometric geometry on ScanNet++ scene 7e09430da7. Existing benchmark settings remain unchanged; Table 4 newly discloses view counts rather than reporting revised sample sizes.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds a three-setting temperature-sensitivity study, a one-scene geometry ablation and illustrated failure analysis (Figures 9–11). These are limited diagnostic extensions; the existing model-complexity, aggregation and prediction-count ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new assignment-entropy plot diagnoses optimization behavior, rather than estimating uncertainty in reported experimental performance.

E6.justification: V2 adds entropy-convergence curves, qualitative evidence of similar albedo under two geometry sources, and failure examples. Existing Tables 1–3 are unchanged: for example, Table 1 retains IIF albedo PSNR 20.72, SSIM 0.846 and LPIPS 0.201. These additions do not establish improved benchmark performance.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations 1–12 are unchanged apart from presentation. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption or derivation is introduced; the temperature study supplies empirical diagnostics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about combining single-view priors with constrained inverse rendering to obtain consistent materials and outperform existing reconstruction methods.

C2.justification: V2 explains the temperature tradeoff between premature hard assignment and oversmoothing, and interprets the geometry comparison as evidence of tolerance to lower-quality geometry. It also makes limitations more specific: missing thin structures, transparent objects, floating artifacts and consistently incorrect material predictions can contaminate reconstruction.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds Table 4 identifying nine previously used scenes and their view counts, such as Kitchen with 202 views and Bedroom with 208. It also explicitly summarizes evaluation averaging. Existing implementation settings, hardware, timings and access information are retained.

R1.justification: The same 35 cited works and the same related-work positioning are retained. New supplementary passages reuse existing references; reference backlinks and figure numbering changes do not alter research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 makes small table-caption clarifications, adds a dataset-details paragraph and organizes Appendix B into named discussion topics. The main narrative and section structure remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds the dataset table and temperature, geometry and failure-case displays, with localized appendix reflow. Earlier supplementary Figures 9–13 are retained as Figures 12–16. Main figures and table structures remain unchanged, with small caption and equation-layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: Table 4 improves documentation of the evaluation data, while Figures 9–11 make the temperature choice, geometry sensitivity and concrete failure conditions easier to assess. These provide useful but limited gains: the geometry evidence is qualitative and confined to one scene, and the method, established benchmark results and statistical reporting remain unchanged.
